name: Hotels
h1: AI Phone Agent for Hotels: Front Desk Overflow Calls
metaDescription: Calldesk answers hotel calls when the front desk is busy: room inquiries, amenity and policy questions, group requests and late-night guest calls.
intro: A hotel front desk has two audiences at once: guests standing at the counter and callers on the phone. At check-in time, mid-afternoon, a line forms at the desk and the phone rings anyway. Callers want to know if there are rooms for a certain weekend, whether pets are welcome, what time breakfast ends, where to park a truck, and whether the shuttle runs to the airport. Overnight, the desk is thinly staffed, and in-house guests call about a noisy hallway, a missing towel, or how to reach the front desk from the room phone. Group sales and event inquiries call too, and need someone senior. The costs of a missed call are asymmetric. A prospective guest who hears nothing books elsewhere, while an in-house guest who cannot get through is unhappy right away. A Calldesk agent can answer as the hotel's AI assistant, handle policy and amenity questions from a knowledge base, take a reservation inquiry and pass it to staff, transfer in-house guest requests to the desk or night manager, and route group requests to sales. It does not quote live rates or confirm room inventory unless you connect a source of truth, and it should say so. After hours it can take messages and log requests.
callTypes: Prospective guests asking about room types, pet policy and parking
Same-night travelers calling for availability after a flight delay
In-house guests requesting towels, a late checkout or a maintenance fix
Group and wedding-block inquiries meant for the sales office
Questions about breakfast hours, pool access, airport shuttle and check-in times
Overnight calls about noise or security that need the manager on duty

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thank you for calling the hotel. I'm the hotel's AI assistant. Are you a guest staying with us, or planning a visit?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Planning one. Do you allow dogs?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Dogs are welcome in designated rooms on the ground floor. There is a pet fee listed on our website policy page. Would you like me to pass your details to the reservations team?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Yes. I'd like two nights next weekend.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I can't confirm live availability or rates myself, so the reservations team will check and call you back. May I have your name and number?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Kenji Watanabe, and use this number.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks, Kenji. What dates, and how many guests and dogs?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Friday to Sunday, two adults and one small dog.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Got it. Would you like a ground-floor room, since that's where dogs are allowed? I'll note it as a request.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: All noted. You can expect a call from reservations; they will go over the rate and the pet policy before booking.

setupSteps: Create an agent from the receptionist template, with the hotel name, address and a statement of what it can and cannot confirm.
Fill the knowledge base with room types, amenities, pet and parking policies, shuttle times, breakfast hours and check-in and check-out times.
Define separate paths for prospective guests, in-house guests and group sales, with transfers to the desk, night manager or sales office.
Add extraction fields for dates, party size, room preferences and callback number, and send them by webhook to your reservations team.
Test overnight and daytime scenarios, publish on the front desk line or its overflow, and review live calls during the first weekend.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Answers repeat policy and amenity questions so the desk is not interrupted during check-in.
Moves in-house requests to the desk or night manager and group inquiries to sales.
Captures stay dates, party size and preferences for reservations to follow up.
Handles callers in other languages on the Standard and Pro voices, which helps hotels with international visitors.
Leaves a summary for the morning manager covering overnight calls and open requests.

considerations: Guest names, room numbers and payment details are sensitive. Decide what the agent may ask for, and avoid collecting card numbers by phone unless you have reviewed your payment-security obligations.
Do not let the agent state live rates or confirm availability unless it is connected to a source you trust; a wrong answer creates a booking dispute.
Security or safety emergencies reported by phone should be passed to a human and emergency services without delay. Test that path.
If you record or transcribe calls, check consent requirements where guests and staff are located, and update your privacy notices as needed.

faq.a: Not by default. It has no built-in link to hotel property systems. You could connect a function step to your own endpoint, but plan that as an integration project.
Calldesk supports 40+ languages, though Lite's voice speaks English. Standard or Pro is required for non-English speech.

faq.q: What happens when a guest calls from their room?
faq.a: You can add a path that recognizes in-house guests and transfers to the desk, or logs a request such as a towel delivery for staff to complete.

faq.q: Can it handle wedding or group block inquiries?
faq.a: It collects the event date, size and contact details and passes the inquiry to sales. Quotes and contracts stay with your team.

faq.q: Do I need to replace my phone system?
faq.a: No. You can forward overflow or after-hours calls to a Calldesk number, or bring your own carrier for the number the agent answers.
